Your spaceship just left without you, and you're lost on a planet.
With no real atmosphere, the day side hits eight hundred degrees Fahrenheit.
Then at night, it drops to about minus two hundred ninety.
You'd be cooked, then frozen, with no air to complain about it.
Jupiter has no ground at all, only swirling gas and liquid, getting denser as you sink.
You can't land. You just fall, and the pressure climbs.
Neptune has no surface either, and it's the windiest world in the solar system.
Its winds top twelve hundred miles an hour, about nine times Earth's.
Venus has an actual ground, which sounds nice, until you stand on it.
It's about eight hundred seventy degrees Fahrenheit, hot enough to melt lead.
The air presses on you ninety-three times harder than on Earth, like a kilometer underwater, under sulfuric acid clouds.
So where would you rather get lost? Please say Earth.
